messages:
pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident PD-987654 triggered on service `data-ingest-prod` (high) — unacknowledged. Escalation policy: default-night. Link: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-987654
Alex W: ugh I just got paged, not on this rotation. Did someone trigger a manual page?
Maria C: same, got the alert at 03:12am, I’m on rotation for infra, not data-ingest.
Ryan (oncall): I pulled the PD link — it shows service `data-ingest-prod` and the trigger tag `team:data-ingest`. I think that tag was recently added to an alert rule.
SRE Lead - Priya: Ok, hold. If this is misrouted we should silence the wrong service and page the correct owners. @pagerduty-admin can you mute the active escalation while we triage? :pray:
pagerduty-admin: Applying a 1h maintenance_override to `data-ingest-prod` now, reason: misrouted page.
Alex W: thanks. Can someone post the routing rule that fired? I want to see if this was a tag or schedule mismatch.
pagerduty-admin: Looks like the alert came from our monitoring cluster with metadata: `service_tag=data-ingest, env=prod, region=us-west-2`. Routing rules show: `if service_tag == "data-ingest" -> route to service data-ingest-staging` but there is a fallback that maps unknown tag+prod -> `data-ingest-prod`. There was a recent terraform change that added the tag to the staging mapping but the prod fallback remained.
Ryan (oncall): Here's the snippet from the Terraform routing module I pulled from the PR history:```hcl
module "pd_routing" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/routing.git//modules/pd"
  mappings = {
    "data-ingest" = "service.data-ingest-staging"
  }
  fallback = "service.data-ingest-prod"
}
```
Maria C: So the tag exists, but because the alert had `env=prod`, the staging mapping didn't match and PD fell back to prod service. That explains why production people got woken up.
SRE Lead - Priya: Right. Two issues: routing lacks env-aware mappings, and the alert emission includes ambiguous tag. Immediate mitigation: change PD routing to prefer env-specific service mapping, and update alert emitter to send `service=data-ingest` + `deployment=staging` explicitly for staging alerts.
Alex W: For now I pushed a temporary mapping in PD: `data-ingest|prod -> service.data-ingest-oncall` to direct pages to the correct owners. I used the PD UI to add rule with higher priority.
pagerduty-admin: Confirmed temporary rule added. Also removed escalation override. Current state: suppression active on original prod incident; new test alert fired to `data-ingest-oncall` succeeded.
oncall-bot: Test page: incident PD-987655 triggered on service `data-ingest-oncall` — acknowledged by Maria C.
Maria C: Got and acknowledged the test. Looks good.
Ryan (oncall): We should revert the temporary mapping after the config fix. I've opened a PR to update the TF routing module to use composite key `${service_tag}:${env}` and added unit tests for matching. PR: https://git.redwood.com/routing/pulls/431
SRE Lead - Priya: Excellent. Action items: 1) PagerDuty routing change to be moved into infra as code (PR 431) — Ryan; 2) Update monitoring alert metadata to include `deployment` key — Alex; 3) Postmortem and runbook update for routing mismatches — Priya. Please tag me on the postmortem.
Alex W: Quick note for on-call: if you get a page and it looks wrong, please acknowledge+suppress rather than escalate — that prevents a page storm.
Maria C: Adding one more: schedule timezones — the new schedule added last month had America/Los_Angeles while some services expect UTC; I suspect mismatch made the fallback fire during night. We should standardize schedules.
SRE Lead - Priya: Agreed. Add timezone standardization to the postmortem.
Ryan (oncall): I merged PR 431 and kicked off a deployment to staging routing. Plan to promote to prod after validation.
pagerduty-admin: Temporary mapping removed. Maintenance window cleared.
Alex W: closing the thread for now; file created for postmortem PD-987654-rtg-misconfig; assign to Priya. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
